I could not refute the row. Clause by clause, the printed definition (excerpt lines 2-6 = d1_setup.tex 316-320) and the Lean `CV.Diagrammatic` (statement file lines 1311-1317, restated verbatim in the `diagrammatic` field at 1623-1629) denote the same class on n >= 3.

Mapping checked to primitives (all SM primitives, `open SM`, no CV-local redefinitions of `incident`/`edgeSegment`/`edgePoint`/`det`):
1. "A polygon P" -> `IsPolygon P` = `forall i, edge P i != 0` (def:polygon's p_{i+1} != p_i).
2. "its self-intersections are finitely many" -> `(selfIntersections P).Finite`, where a self-intersection is a plane point with two distinct preimages under the traversal parametrization `(i, s)`, `0 <= s < 1` |-> `p_i + s d_i` (lines 1283-1298). The half-open interval means each corner p_{i+1} is named once, by `(i+1, 0)`, never by `(i, 1)`, so a simple corner is not a self-intersection. Each edge contributes at most one preimage per point (injective since d_i != 0), so finiteness of points and of crossing pairs coincide.
3. "isolated" -> derived from finiteness (`isolated` field, lines 1631-1632); the printed also demands finiteness, so no content is lost or added.
4. "transverse crossing of two edges with exactly two preimages" -> `exists i j s t, i != j /\ preimages P x = {(i,s),(j,t)} /\ det (edge P i) (edge P j) != 0`. `i != j` is redundant (two distinct parameters on one nonzero edge give distinct points). Together with clause 6, s,t in (0,1), i.e. an interior transverse crossing of two edges.
5. "no two of them sharing an image or a preimage" -> under the points reading it is vacuous; under the crossing-pairs reading it is exactly "no triple point", which `preimages P x = {(i,s),(j,t)}` (a two-element set) enforces. Mechanical check on the printed triple point ((-3,0),(3,0),(0,-3),(0,3),(-2,-2),(2,2)): Lean preimages of (0,0) are (0,1/2),(2,1/2),(4,1/2); every other Lean clause (IsPolygon, Finite, no corner, vertex clause) is satisfied and only this clause fails -- matching the printed remark that this clause "is not implied by the others". Both reject.
6. "none of them at a corner" -> `forall x in selfIntersections P, forall i, x != P i`.
7. "no vertex of P lying on an edge not incident to it" -> `forall i e, not incident i e -> P i notin edgeSegment P e`, with SM `incident v e := e = v-1 \/ e = v` (the two edges e_{v-1}, e_v at p_v) and `edgeSegment` the closed segment t in [0,1], matching the printed closed edges e_i = [p_i, p_{i+1}].

Concrete agreement tests (Python evaluation of the Lean clauses as read): printed exterior-collinear ((0,0),(2,0),(1,0),(0,1)) -> Lean rejects (Finite fails via the e_0/e_1 overlap, corner clause fails at (1,0) with preimages (0,1/2),(2,0), vertex clause fails: p_2 on e_0), printed says not diagrammatic. T-contact ((0,0),(4,0),(4,2),(2,0),(0,2)), vertex p_3 touching remote edge e_0 tangentially -> Lean rejects (corner clause and vertex clause), printed rejects by the vertex clause. Interior flat turn ((0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(2,2),(0,2)) -> both accept ("So is the polygon at a simple positive flat wall ... middle vertex inside the segment"). Bow-tie ((0,0),(2,2),(2,0),(0,2)) -> both accept. Coincident remote vertices p_i = p_j, and p_i = p_{i+2}: both sides reject via the vertex clause (p_i lies on the closed non-incident edge e_j / e_{i+1}). A genuinely tangential edge-edge contact without a vertex is impossible for segments (collinear => overlap => infinitely many self-intersections, rejected by both).

Non-refuting observations: (a) `Diagrammatic` carries no `3 <= n` hypothesis (inherited from `IsPolygon`); for n = 0 an injective infinite path is vacuously `Diagrammatic`. This is a domain widening, not a narrowing, and for the printed n >= 3 the notions agree. (b) The bundle records `of_weak` (SM WeakGeneric -> Diagrammatic) and `iff_crossing_geometry` (F3), which have no sentence in d1_setup.tex 315-344; they are relations to accepted SM notions, permitted by the brief, and do not alter what `Diagrammatic` denotes.
